drills.title: Totals by category
drills.prompt: Arrange the lines so the program adds up the expenses per category. The empty map may be created at any point before the loop. Two lines do not belong.
lines: List<Expense> list = List.of(new Expense("Food", 1500), new Expense("Fun", 99.5), new Expense("Food", 300));
drills.explain: merge(key, value, Double::sum) means: if the category has no total yet, store the amount, otherwise add it to the old total. put would overwrite the earlier Food total with the last amount, and merge needs all three arguments. A TreeMap prints its keys sorted A to Z.

drills.title: Line up the money
drills.prompt: Fill the format patterns so the program prints the goal output. Locale.US keeps the decimal point and commas the same on every computer.
drills.explain: In a format pattern, - left-aligns, the number is the minimum width, a comma adds thousands separators and .2 gives two decimals: %-8s, %,9.2f. A single % always starts a format code, so a real percent sign is written %%.

drills.title: Budget status at the borders
drills.prompt: Read the code and type exactly what it prints, one line per line of output.
code: static String status(double spent, double limit) {
drills.explain: The chain is checked from left to right. 75% is below 80, so OK. 1600 is exactly 80%, and >= includes the border, so WARN. Spending exactly the limit is not over it (> is strict), so it is still WARN. Only 2000.5 passes the limit. When you read a boundary check, test the exact border value.

drills.title: One monthly total for everything
drills.prompt: The program should print one total per month (2026-11 and 2026-12), but it prints a single total. Click the faulty line, then choose the fix.
code: List<Expense> expenses = List.of(new Expense("2026-11-02", 1500), new Expense("2026-11-10", 1200),
fixed_code: List<Expense> expenses = List.of(new Expense("2026-11-02", 1500), new Expense("2026-11-10", 1200),
drills.explain: substring(start, end) stops before end. "2026-11-02".substring(0, 6) is "2026-1", so November and December both become the key 2026-1 and are added together. The month key "2026-11" has 7 characters, so the end index is 7. Using 5 to 7 would give only "11" and "12" and lose the year, and 8 would keep the dash.

issues.text: add stores any amount, even a negative one, and always returns true
issues.why: The tracker must reject amounts of 0 or less and tell the caller (return false). Here the -300 slips in and silently reduces every total.
Without a Locale the computer's own settings decide the separators, so the same line can print 1.200,00 on one machine and 1,200.00 on another. Pass Locale.US as the first argument.
== checks for the same object, not the same letters. It happens to work for literals typed in the same program, but a category read with Scanner would never match. Use e.category().equals(category).

non_issues.text: Money should be a BigDecimal, so double is wrong here
non_issues.why: BigDecimal is what real banks use, but for a learning tracker double is fine, as the lesson says. It is not a bug in this code.

non_issues.text: percent > 100 should be >= 100, because spending the whole limit is already over
non_issues.why: Spending exactly the limit is not over it. The strict comparison matches the rule "OVER means spent is greater than the limit".

non_issues.text: The list should be a static field so every method can see it
non_issues.why: Passing the list into each method is the better design. It avoids global state and keeps the methods easy to test.

drills.explain: In generated project code look for missing validation, locale-dependent formatting and == between texts. Those pass a quick demo and fail with real data.
